description: This bar chart, titled “Quality Scores,” illustrates the performance of three different metrics—IFD, TagNum, and DEITA—across two types of average scores: Avg_obj (object-level, shown in light blue) and Avg_sub (subject-level, shown in light orange), as evaluated in the context of automatic data selection for instruction tuning via maximizing information gain in semantic space. The vertical y-axis, labeled “Scores,” ranges from 30 to 70 in increments of 5, representing the numerical score values. For each metric on the x-axis, two bars are displayed side by side: the taller light blue bar corresponds to Avg_obj, and the shorter light orange bar corresponds to Avg_sub. Specifically, IFD scores 63.98 (Avg_obj) and 41.90 (Avg_sub); TagNum scores 66.06 (Avg_obj) and 39.13 (Avg_sub); and DEITA scores 67.64 (Avg_obj) and 42.99 (Avg_sub). Two horizontal reference lines are overlaid: a dashed blue line at 64.71 labeled “Base Avg_obj,” and a dashed orange line at 37.91 labeled “Base Avg_sub,” indicating baseline averages for comparison. The chart visually demonstrates that DEITA achieves the highest Avg_obj score, while TagNum has the lowest Avg_sub score, with all Avg_obj scores exceeding their respective Avg_sub scores.
